speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand what is connecting these symptoms, have you noticed any fever, redness, or warmth in your knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome) due to an undiagnosed sexually transmitted infection, such as Chlamydia trachomatis. The clinical triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle and knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and the patient's sexual history is highly suggestive. I will request a Urine culture and Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea, along with inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and HLA-B27 testing to confirm.
